data.stem: Which official is the de jure executive of a state under the parliamentary system?
data.explanation: The Governor is correct: he is the nominal, or de jure, executive and head of the state. The Chief Minister is the de facto executive and head of the government, while the Speaker and the Advocate-General have roles in the legislature and in law, so those options are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which Article provides that the Chief Minister shall be appointed by the Governor?
data.explanation: Article 164 is correct; it says the Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor, while other ministers are appointed on the Chief Minister's advice. Article 163 creates the council to aid the Governor, Article 166 covers conduct of business and Article 167 covers the Chief Minister's duty to inform, so those are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Under the parliamentary convention, whom must the Governor call to form the government when one party has a clear majority?
options: A nominee of the Chief Secretary
The leader of the majority party
data.explanation: The leader of the majority party is correct; convention requires the Governor to appoint that leader as Chief Minister. The leader of the opposition, a nominee of the Chief Secretary and an MLA chosen by lot are not what the convention requires, so those options are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Whose pleasure does the Chief Minister's term depend on?
data.explanation: The Governor's is correct: the Chief Minister holds office during the Governor's pleasure, though that does not allow dismissal while he has majority support. The President, the Chief Justice and the Speaker have no such role in the Chief Minister's tenure, so those options are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: A non-legislator appointed Chief Minister must get elected to the state legislature within how many months?
data.explanation: Six months is correct; if he is not elected in that period he ceases to be Chief Minister. One month, three months and twelve months are not the period the chapter gives for this, so those options are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem:
Consider the following statements about the appointment of a Chief Minister:
1. The Constitution lays down a detailed selection procedure.
2. The Governor may appoint first and ask for proof of majority later.
3. A non-legislator may hold the office for six months while seeking election.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
data.explanation: 2 and 3 only is correct. The Constitution has no detailed selection procedure, so statement 1 is wrong and options including it are incorrect. The Governor may appoint first and ask for proof of majority within a reasonable period, and a non-legislator may serve for six months while getting elected.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which option comes first in the Sarkaria order when no single party has an absolute majority?
options: A post-election coalition with all partners in government
The largest single party seeking outside support
A post-election alliance with outside support
data.explanation: A pre-election alliance of parties is correct: it is first in the order when no party has an absolute majority. The largest single party comes third, while the two post-election options come after it, so those options are wrong in that order.
data.label: practice

data.stem: According to the Sarkaria Commission, within how many days must a Chief Minister who is not from an absolute-majority party seek a vote of confidence?
data.explanation: 30 days is correct: the Sarkaria Commission recommended a vote of confidence within 30 days of taking over. Seven, sixty and ninety days are not the recommended period, so those options are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: When may a Governor dismiss a Chief Minister, according to the chapter?
options: Only after the Chief Minister loses majority support in the Assembly
Whenever he disagrees with the Chief Minister's policy
Whenever the Chief Minister is absent from a session
Whenever the Chief Minister travels outside the state
data.explanation: Only after the Chief Minister loses majority support in the Assembly is correct: a Chief Minister with majority support cannot be dismissed, and once he loses confidence he must resign or be dismissed. Disagreement with policy, absence and travel are not grounds the chapter describes, so those options are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which oath commits the Chief Minister not to reveal matters that come to him as a state minister?
options: The oath of allegiance to the party
The oath of loyalty to the Governor
data.explanation: The oath of secrecy is correct: it binds the holder not to reveal matters that come to him as minister, except as his duties require. The oath of office concerns allegiance, faithful duty and fair treatment; the party and Governor oaths are not in the chapter, so those options are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem:
Consider the following statements about collective responsibility under Article 164:
1. The council of ministers is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly.
2. A minister who disagrees with a cabinet decision may ignore it and stay in office.
3. Cabinet decisions bind every minister, even those who dissented in the meeting.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
data.explanation: 1 and 3 only is correct. Article 164 makes the council collectively responsible to the Assembly, and cabinet decisions bind every minister even if one dissented in the meeting. Statement 2 is wrong: a minister who cannot defend a cabinet decision must resign, so options including 2 are incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which of the following appointments does the Chief Minister advise the Governor on?
data.explanation: The Advocate-General of the state is correct: the Chief Minister advises the Governor on this and on posts such as state public service commission members and the state election commissioner. The Chief Justice of India, another state's Governor and the Union Finance Minister are not appointments the chapter places under his advice, so those options are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which Article gives ministers the right to speak in the Houses of the state legislature, though they vote only in the House they belong to?
data.explanation: Article 177 is correct: it lets every minister speak and take part in House proceedings and committees, though he may vote only in the House he belongs to. Articles 163 and 164 concern the council and appointments, and Article 166 covers conduct of government business, so those options are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem:
Consider the following statements about the Chief Minister's powers:
1. Advice to end the Assembly before its term can be tendered by the Chief Minister whenever he chooses.
2. The State Planning Board is headed by the Chief Minister.
3. He heads the Inter-State Council as its presiding chair.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
data.explanation: 1 and 2 only is correct. The Chief Minister may recommend dissolution at any time and chairs the State Planning Board. Statement 3 is wrong: he is a member of the Inter-State Council, which the Prime Minister heads, so options that include 3 are incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem:
Consider the following statements about the size of a state council of ministers:
1. Ministers, including the Chief Minister, may not exceed 15 per cent of the Assembly strength.
2. Ministers, including the Chief Minister, may not be fewer than 12.
3. These limits were introduced by the 94th Amendment Act of 2006.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
data.explanation: 1 and 2 only is correct. The 15 per cent ceiling and the minimum of 12 were added by the 91st Amendment Act of 2003. Statement 3 is wrong because the 94th Amendment dealt with the tribal welfare minister for Bihar, so options including 3 are incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem: What happens when the Legislative Assembly passes a no-confidence motion against the state council of ministers?
options: Only ministers who sit in the Assembly resign
All ministers resign, including those in the Legislative Council
The council is suspended until the next budget session
data.explanation: All ministers resign, including those in the Legislative Council, is correct, since collective responsibility means the whole council falls together. The other options do not match the chapter: resignation is not limited to the Chief Minister or to Assembly members, and the council is not suspended.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Whose advice does the Governor act on when removing a minister, in keeping with individual responsibility?
data.explanation: The Chief Minister is correct: the Governor removes a minister only on the Chief Minister's advice, which is the basis of individual responsibility. The Speaker, the Chief Secretary and a party president have no such role under the chapter, so those options are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: In Shamsher Singh (1974), whose satisfaction is meant where the Constitution requires the Governor's satisfaction?
data.explanation: The council of ministers' satisfaction is correct; the court held that the Governor's satisfaction is in substance the council's, not his personal view. The Governor's personal satisfaction, the Chief Justice's and the Speaker's are not what the court held, so those options are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: What does Article 163 say about the advice that ministers give to the Governor?
options: It cannot be enquired into in any court
It must be published in the official gazette
It may be challenged in any court
It binds the Governor only when the Assembly sits
data.explanation: It cannot be enquired into in any court is correct, which underlines the confidential relationship between Governor and ministers. Gazette publication and court challenge are not what the Article says, and a rule binding only when the Assembly sits has no basis in it, so those options are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which state was freed from the tribal welfare minister requirement by the 94th Amendment Act of 2006?
data.explanation: Bihar is correct: the 94th Amendment freed it from the obligation, since Bihar has no Scheduled Areas now and a small Scheduled Tribe population. Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand and Odisha still must have a tribal welfare minister, so those options are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem:
Consider the following statements about the state council of ministers:
1. Ministers of state always attend cabinet meetings.
2. Deputy ministers are not given independent charge of departments.
3. The cabinet is the nucleus of the council of ministers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
data.explanation: 2 and 3 only is correct. Deputy ministers are attached to cabinet ministers without independent charge, and the cabinet is the nucleus of the council. Ministers of state attend cabinet only when specially invited, so statement 1 is wrong and options including it are incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem: At which level of government is the word 'ministry' used, according to the chapter?
options: Equally at the Centre and in the states
data.explanation: Only at the Centre is correct: the chapter notes that states have departments, not ministries. Use at the state level, in district administration and equal use at both tiers are not what the chapter says, so those options are wrong.
data.label: practice
